title: Restored schema22 state can lose the bootstrapped Owner and still be reported verified
evidence: At bootstrap22 the runner checks one auth_principals row. At verify22 it checks only ledger/integrity/foreign keys and typed-empty session/queue; it never compares the restored schema hash or table row hashes to sealed22. A pure synthetic 1..22 ledger with auth_principals.count=0 passes validate_ledger(...,22). The status can become PUBLIC22_BASELINE_VERIFIED_PENDING_ROOT_REVIEW although restore did not preserve the created Owner.
required_change: For verify22, compare restored schema hash and complete expected table count/row-hash map to sealed22 (or explicitly verify all intended preserved rows, including auth_principals and domain_objects) before success. Retain truthful partial and failure receipts on mismatch.

title: Preparation filesystem failure can leave a partial output root without runner failure receipt
evidence: require_phase(prepare), output ancestor check, root.mkdir and four subdirectory mkdir calls occur before state is created and before try/except/finally. A failure after root.mkdir but before try leaves a partial root without first_failure, publication, recoverability or case.closed.json. The Root caller may capture the outer original, but this leaf cannot claim its own phase-level failure receipt for that interval.
required_change: Place preparation side effects under the same failure/cleanup receipt boundary or emit an explicit pre-run Root failure record that identifies the path and partial publication. Do not fabricate a child exit.
